newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-GUINEAS WINNERS CLASH AGAIN IN PRIX DU MOULIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-GUINEAS WINNERS CLASH AGAIN IN PRIX DU MOULIN.

text.p: French and Irish 2,000 Guineas winners Ashkalani and Spinning World clash for the third time this season in the Group One Prix du Moulin at Longhchamp on Sunday.
The big Parisian event is one of France's top mile (1.6 km) events and Spinning World will be hoping to make it third time lucky after twice losing out to the French colt.

Spinning World was thought to be unlucky in the French 2,000 Guineas, and had a valid excuse for his defeat in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, a race in which Ashkalani also tasted defeat for the first time, surrendering his unbeaten record to the game Bijou d'Inde when Mick Kinane replaced the suspended Gerald Mosse in the saddle.
Kinane was criticised for getting to the front too soon, while Spinning World, tackling his third consecutive Group One event faded to finish sixth.
The third meeting between the pair was to have taken place in the Group One Prix Jacques le Marois at Deauville last month, but Ashakalani was pulled out when the rains came.
Spinning World, refreshed after a break, bounced back to form to win that race in the colours of the Niarchos Family in good style, with Vetheuil and Shaanxi his immediate victims.
Spinning World will contest Sunday's race with a pacemaker, Metaphor, with Vetheuil and Shaanxi again in opposition.
The Japanese-owned filly, Shaanxi, second in the Moulin last year to Ridgewood Pearl, has clearly returned to her best after dull spell.
Shake The Yoke, winner of the the group one Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot, adds spice to an intriguing contest.
The Elie Lellouche runner, unlucky not to have won the French 1,000 Guineas in the spring, races for the first time in the colours of American B Wayne Hughes following her sale in the summer.
